knowledge_point.title: Reconstructing a Three-Variable Function From Its Gradient

question.:question/problem:
Find $f(x,y,z)$ such that $\nabla f(x,y,z)=\mathbf{F}(x,y,z),$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)&=\left(- 2 y\right)\,\mathbf{i} \\ &{}+\left(- 2 x + z\right)\,\mathbf{j} \\ &{}+\left(y - 1\right)\,\mathbf{k}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the function $f(x,y,z)$ is defined as

$$
\nabla f(x,y,z)=\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\,\mathbf{i}+\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\,\mathbf{j}+\frac{\partial f}{\partial z}\,\mathbf{k}.
$$

Since $\nabla f(x,y,z)=\mathbf{F}(x,y,z),$ the function $f(x,y,z)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=- 2 y \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}&=- 2 x + z \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial z}&=y - 1\end{aligned}
$$

First, we integrate $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y$ and $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z)&=\int \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=\int \left(- 2 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=- 2 x y+g(y,z)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to $y,$ we obtain

$$
\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}=- 2 x+\frac{\partial g}{\partial y}.
$$

Taking $\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}=- 2 x + z$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}- 2 x+\frac{\partial g}{\partial y}&=- 2 x + z \\ \frac{\partial g}{\partial y}&=z\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate $\frac{\partial g}{\partial y}$ with respect to $y.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}g(y,z)&=\int \frac{\partial g}{\partial y}\,\mathrm{d}y \\ &=\int \left(z\right)\,\mathrm{d}y \\ &=y z+h(z)\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $g(y,z)=y z+h(z)$ in the expression for $f(x,y,z),$ we get

$$
f(x,y,z)=- 2 x y + y z+h(z).
$$

To determine the function $h(z),$ we differentiate $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z.$ This gives

$$
\frac{\partial f}{\partial z}=y+h'(z).
$$

Comparing this derivative with the third component and subtracting the known terms gives

$$
\begin{aligned}h'(z)&=-1 \\ h(z)&=- z+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a constant.

Consequently,

$$
f(x,y,z)=- 2 x y + y z - z+C.
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: f(x,y,z)=- 2 x y + 2 y z - 2 z+C
f(x,y,z)=- 2 x y + y z - z+C
f(x,y,z)=- 2 x y - 2 y z + 2 z+C
